바다.x: I swim in the sea in summer.

운전.e: Literally 'move and turn'. 운전하다 = to drive.

소파.x: My father is watching TV on the sofa.
소파.t: Korean has no f sound, so English f becomes ㅍ: sofa → 소파, coffee → 커피.

팔다.forms: 팔아요 · 팔았어요 · 팔 거예요 · 파세요 (ㄹ drops)
팔다.x: Do they sell milk at this store?
팔다.e: Opposite of 사다 (buy). 팔 also means 'arm' and 'eight'.
팔다.t: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ: 파세요, 파는 사람 (seller).

조금.forms: short form: 좀 · 조금 + verb/adjective: 조금 어려워요
조금.m: a little, a bit; a little while
조금.x: I can speak a little Korean.
조금.e: Shortened to 좀 in everyday speech.

제일.forms: 제일 + adjective: 제일 좋아요 · (noun) 중에서 제일 …
제일.x: I like kimchi stew the most.
제일.t: Pattern: A 중에서 B가 제일 … = 'Among A, B is the most …'.

안전하다.ex: 이 동네는 밤에도 안전해서 걱정 없어요.
안전하다.x: This neighborhood is safe even at night, so there's nothing to worry about.

선글라스.x: The sunlight was strong, so I put on sunglasses.
선글라스.e: From English 'sunglasses'; count it as one item: 선글라스 하나.
선글라스.t: Glasses and sunglasses take the verb 쓰다, not 입다: 선글라스를 쓰다.

수준.ex: 제 수준에 맞는 책을 찾고 있어요.
수준.x: I'm looking for a book that fits my level.
수준.e: Literally 'water level' — like a carpenter's level.
수준.t: Common collocations: 수준이 높다/낮다 'the level is high/low'.

출근.m: going to work, getting to work
출근.ex: 출근 시간에는 지하철에 사람이 정말 많아요.
출근.x: The subway is really crowded during rush hour.

실례지만.m: excuse me, but …; sorry to bother you, but …
실례지만.ex: 실례지만 이 근처에 화장실이 어디에 있어요?
실례지만.x: Excuse me, but where is a restroom around here?
실례지만.e: Literally 'it's a lapse of manners, but …'.
실례지만.t: Perfect for polite openers to strangers, e.g. 실례지만 성함이 어떻게 되세요? 'May I ask your name?'

주로.forms: 주로 + verb; 주로 뭐 해요? = What do you usually do?
주로.x: On weekends I mostly watch movies at home.

수영복.x: I bought a new swimsuit to go to the beach.
수영복.t: Many Koreans wear a 래시가드 'rash guard' at the beach for sun protection, and indoor pools usually require a swim cap (수영모) as well.

퇴원하다.m: to be discharged from (the) hospital, to leave the hospital
퇴원하다.x: I left the hospital a week after my surgery.

보도.ex: 뉴스 보도에 따르면 내일 큰 태풍이 온다고 합니다.
보도.x: According to news reports, a big typhoon is coming tomorrow.
보도.e: Literally 'report and tell.' Homonym 보도 also means sidewalk.
보도.t: 보도에 따르면 'according to reports' is a very common news phrase.

반대.x: The plan was canceled because many people opposed it.
반대.t: 반대 also means 'opposite': 반대 방향 'the opposite direction', 반대말 'antonym.'

미신.ex: 밤에 손톱을 깎으면 안 된다는 것은 미신이에요.
미신.x: The idea that you shouldn't cut your nails at night is a superstition.
미신.t: A famous Korean superstition: writing a living person's name in red ink is bad luck.

거절.x: I asked my friend a favor, but I got turned down.
거절.t: 거절을 당하다 = to be rejected or turned down.

의지.ex: 그는 강한 의지로 병을 이겨 냈어요.
의지.x: He beat the illness through sheer willpower.
의지.t: A homonym 의지 means 'reliance', as in 의지하다 'to lean on someone'.

섬세하다.ex: 그 디자이너는 아주 섬세한 작품을 만들어요.
섬세하다.x: That designer makes very delicate work.
섬세하다.e: Literally 'fine and thin', like delicate threads.

두근두근.x: It's my first date, so my heart is pounding.
두근두근.e: Manner word (의태어) for a heart beating fast and hard from excitement, nerves or fear.
두근두근.t: The verb 두근거리다 is very common: 가슴이 두근거려요 'My heart is racing.'

수익성.ex: 이 사업은 수익성이 낮아서 그만두기로 했어요.
수익성.x: We decided to drop this business because its profitability was low.
수익성.e: -성 = quality of being: 수익성, 가능성, 안전성.
수익성.t: Pronounced [수익썽] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

난민.ex: 전쟁 때문에 많은 사람들이 난민이 되었습니다.
난민.x: Many people became refugees because of the war.

개인주의.x: Individualism is growing stronger in cities.
개인주의.t: 개인주의 is neutral (valuing the individual), while 이기주의 is negative (selfishness).

재방송.ex: 어제 못 본 드라마를 재방송으로 봤어요.
재방송.x: I watched the drama I missed yesterday as a rerun.
재방송.e: 재- 'again' + 방송 'broadcast'; 재- = again: 재사용, 재시험.

침몰.ex: 배가 침몰하기 전에 승객들이 모두 구조됐어요.
침몰.x: All the passengers were rescued before the ship sank.

과로.x: My father collapsed from overwork and was hospitalized.
과로.e: Literally 'excessive labor'. 과- = over-, too much: 과식, 과음.
과로.t: 과로사 means 'death from overwork,' a serious social issue in Korea.

작곡가.x: Mozart was a famous 18th-century Austrian composer.

대본.ex: 배우들은 촬영 전에 대본을 여러 번 읽어요.
대본.x: The actors read the script several times before filming.
대본.t: Collocation: 대본을 외우다 'to memorize the script'; 대본 리딩 is a script read-through.

센서.ex: 사람이 지나가면 센서가 반응해서 불이 켜져요.
센서.x: When someone walks by, the sensor reacts and the light turns on.

변호.ex: 그 유명한 변호사가 이 사건의 변호를 맡았어요.
변호.x: That famous lawyer took on the defense in this case.

완고하다.m: stubborn, inflexible, set in one's ways
완고하다.ex: 아버지는 완고해서 생각을 잘 안 바꾸세요.
완고하다.x: My father is set in his ways, so he rarely changes his mind.

연출하다.m: to direct (a film, play); to stage, to create (a scene or mood)
연출하다.ex: 그 감독이 연출한 영화는 모두 인기가 많아요.
연출하다.x: All the movies that director made are very popular.
연출하다.t: Also used for creating a look or mood: 분위기를 연출하다.

허름하다.x: It was a run-down little restaurant, but the food was really delicious.

희미하다.x: My childhood memories are faint now.

눈을 감아 주다.forms: 눈을 감아 줘요 · 눈을 감아 줬어요 · 눈감아 주세요
눈을 감아 주다.m: to turn a blind eye, to let something slide
눈을 감아 주다.ex: 이번 한 번만 눈을 감아 주세요.
눈을 감아 주다.x: Please let it slide just this once.
눈을 감아 주다.e: Literally 'to close one's eyes for someone,' pretending not to see.
눈을 감아 주다.t: The -아 주다 makes it a favor; 눈을 감다 alone means 'to close one's eyes' or even 'to pass away.'

추상적.ex: 그의 설명은 너무 추상적이라서 이해하기 어려웠어요.
추상적.x: His explanation was so abstract that it was hard to understand.
추상적.e: Literally 'drawing out the image': keeping the idea, dropping the details.

철수.x: The government decided to evacuate its citizens living there.
철수.e: Literally 'remove and collect' — pulling people or things out.

돌연변이.ex: 바이러스에 돌연변이가 생겨서 전파력이 더 강해졌습니다.
돌연변이.x: The virus mutated and became more contagious.
돌연변이.e: 돌연 'suddenly' + 변이 'variation' — a sudden change in genes.
돌연변이.t: Pronounced [도련벼니]; each batchim slides into the next vowel.

관여하다.m: to be involved in, to take part in, to have a hand in
관여하다.ex: 그는 이번 프로젝트에 직접 관여하지 않았어요.
관여하다.x: He wasn't directly involved in this project.
관여하다.t: Neutral in tone; 간여하다 often sounds more like meddling.

일탈하다.m: to deviate (from norms), to go astray, to stray
일탈하다.ex: 청소년들이 일탈하지 않도록 관심을 가져야 합니다.
일탈하다.x: We need to pay attention so teenagers don't go astray.
일탈하다.e: Literally 'stray and slip out' — breaking away from social norms.
일탈하다.t: 이탈 = leaving a route or group; 일탈 = breaking rules or routine, e.g. 일상에서의 일탈 'a break from routine'.

애매모호하다.e: Combines 애매 and 모호, both meaning 'unclear'.
애매모호하다.t: Either half works alone; 애매하다 is very common in casual speech.

드문드문.m: sparsely, here and there; now and then
드문드문.x: On weekday afternoons, customers come in only now and then.
드문드문.e: Doubled form built on 드물다 'to be rare'.

띄엄띄엄.ex: 저는 한국어 신문을 아직 띄엄띄엄 읽어요.
띄엄띄엄.x: I still read Korean newspapers haltingly.
띄엄띄엄.e: From 띄다 / 띄우다 'to space apart', as in 띄어쓰기 'word spacing'.
띄엄띄엄.t: Also describes slow, choppy reading or speaking; pronounced [띠엄띠엄].

폐단.m: abuse, corrupt practice, evil (of a system)
폐단.ex: 정부는 오래된 제도의 폐단을 없애려고 합니다.
폐단.x: The government is trying to eliminate the abuses of the old system.
폐단.e: Literally 'ill end' — the bad side that grows out of a practice.
폐단.t: 폐해 is the harm done; 폐단 is the faulty practice or system causing it.

좌파.ex: 좌파와 우파는 복지 정책에 대한 생각이 달라요.
좌파.x: The left and the right have different views on welfare policy.

자율.t: Common compounds: 자율 주행 'self-driving', 자율 학습 'self-study'.

내전.ex: 그 나라는 오랜 내전으로 많은 난민이 생겼습니다.
내전.x: That country's long civil war created many refugees.

외면하다.m: to turn away from, ignore, look away
외면하다.ex: 사람들은 길에서 도움을 청하는 노인을 외면했어요.
외면하다.x: People ignored the elderly man asking for help on the street.
외면하다.e: Literally 'turn the face outward' — away from something.
외면하다.t: Often used with 현실 or 진실: 현실을 외면하다 means 'to ignore reality'.

술회하다.m: to recount (one's feelings or past), to reminisce aloud
술회하다.ex: 그는 인터뷰에서 힘들었던 어린 시절을 술회했습니다.
술회하다.x: In the interview, he recounted his difficult childhood.
술회하다.t: Mostly written or news style, used when someone publicly describes past experiences and feelings.

말단.m: lowest rank, bottom rung; tip, extremity
말단.ex: 그는 말단 사원에서 시작해 사장까지 올랐어요.
말단.x: He started as an entry-level employee and rose to company president.

빈 수레가 요란하다.forms: 빈 수레가 요란하다더니 · 빈 수레가 요란하다고
빈 수레가 요란하다.m: empty vessels make the most noise (lit. an empty cart is noisy)
빈 수레가 요란하다.ex: 빈 수레가 요란하다더니, 자기 자랑만 하던 사람이 실력은 별로였어요.
빈 수레가 요란하다.x: Empty vessels make the most noise: the guy who did nothing but brag about himself wasn't very good.
빈 수레가 요란하다.e: An empty cart rattles and clatters, while a loaded one rolls along quietly.
빈 수레가 요란하다.t: A criticism of people who boast or talk big without real ability. Matches the English 'empty vessels make the most noise'.
nb: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다

파벌.ex: 회사 안에 파벌이 생기면 분위기가 나빠져요.
파벌.x: When cliques form inside a company, the atmosphere goes bad.
파벌.e: Literally 'faction clan' — any closed group, in politics, business or academia.
파벌.t: 파벌 has a negative feel; common phrases are 파벌 싸움 and 파벌을 만들다.

애환.m: joys and sorrows, ups and downs of life
애환.ex: 이 영화는 서민들의 애환을 담고 있습니다.
애환.x: This film captures the joys and sorrows of ordinary people.
애환.t: Collocates with 담다 and 서민, 직장인: the everyday struggles of a group.

갑상선.ex: 이번 건강검진에서 갑상선에 작은 혹이 발견되었어요.
갑상선.x: A small lump was found on my thyroid in this checkup.
갑상선.t: Pronounced [갑쌍선]; the newer official term is 갑상샘, but 갑상선 is far more common.

양성자.ex: 원자핵 속의 양성자는 양전하를 띠고 있습니다.
양성자.x: The protons in an atomic nucleus have a positive charge.
양성자.t: The same 양성 'positive' is used for test results, as in 코로나 양성 (testing positive for COVID).

전자기파.x: Cell phones send and receive information using electromagnetic waves.
전자기파.t: Everyday Korean shortens it to 전자파, as in worries about 전자파 from phones.

가치사슬.ex: 기업은 가치사슬 전체를 분석해서 비용을 줄였습니다.
가치사슬.x: The company cut costs by analyzing its entire value chain.
가치사슬.t: 공급망 'supply chain' is a related but different term often heard in the news.

전위예술.ex: 1960년대에는 많은 젊은 예술가들이 전위예술에 관심을 가졌습니다.
전위예술.x: In the 1960s, many young artists took an interest in avant-garde art.
전위예술.e: Literally 'front-guard art' — art that marches ahead of its time.

천민.m: the lowborn, the lowest social class
천민.ex: 조선 시대에 노비와 백정은 천민으로 취급되었어요.
천민.x: In the Joseon era, slaves and butchers were treated as lowborn.

의병장.m: leader of a righteous army (volunteer militia)
의병장.ex: 곽재우는 임진왜란 때 활약한 유명한 의병장이에요.
의병장.x: Gwak Jae-u is a famous righteous army leader who fought in the Imjin War.

사리.ex: 그 탑 안에서 부처님의 사리가 발견되었어요.
사리.x: The Buddha's relics were found inside that pagoda.
사리.e: A sound borrowing of Sanskrit 'sarira' (body), so the characters' meanings don't help.
사리.t: Don't confuse it with native 사리, a coil of noodles added to a stew, as in 라면 사리.

하지.ex: 하지에는 일 년 중 낮이 가장 길어요.
하지.x: On the summer solstice, the day is the longest of the year.
하지.t: Don't confuse with the verb ending -하지, as in 하지 마세요 ('don't do it').

얄궂다.ex: 얄궂은 운명 때문에 두 사람은 헤어져야 했어요.
얄궂다.x: Because of a cruel twist of fate, the two had to part.
얄궂다.e: Signature collocation: 얄궂은 운명 'a cruel twist of fate'.

주류문화.ex: 한때 비주류였던 웹툰이 이제는 주류문화가 되었습니다.
주류문화.x: Webtoons, once on the fringe, have now become mainstream culture.
주류문화.e: Literally 'main-stream culture', just like the English image.
주류문화.t: Don't confuse 주류 'mainstream' with its homonym 주류 'alcoholic beverages'.

선회하다.m: to circle, to turn around; to shift (a policy)
선회하다.ex: 정부는 강경한 입장에서 대화 쪽으로 선회했습니다.
선회하다.x: The government shifted from a hard-line stance toward dialogue.
선회하다.e: Literally 'revolve and turn', like a plane circling.

재편하다.m: to reorganize, to restructure, to realign
재편하다.ex: 회사는 시장 변화에 맞춰 조직을 재편했습니다.
재편하다.x: The company reorganized its structure to keep up with market changes.
재편하다.e: Literally 'organize again' — reshaping a structure or lineup.

노마지지.ex: 노마지지라고, 선배들의 경험을 무시하면 안 돼요.
노마지지.x: Experience is wisdom, so don't ignore your seniors' know-how.
노마지지.e: An army lost its way and followed an old horse home: experience guides.
